analysis.one_liner: Hindustan Zinc, majority-owned by Vedanta, is India's largest integrated zinc-lead-silver miner and refiner, running mines and smelters mainly in Rajasthan plus a wind power business.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 and H1 FY27 financial results are due on Monday, October 19, 2026, with the earnings call at 4pm IST the same day - two days from now. The production update is already out: Q2 saleable metal output hit a record 264 kt (+7% YoY), refined zinc rose 5% to 212 kt, refined lead 14% to 51 kt, and silver 20% to 173 tonnes, driven by debottlenecking at Chanderiya and Dariba and the new Debari roaster. Separately, parent Vedanta disclosed it has encumbered 50.1% of Hindustan Zinc's share capital to back up to ₹2,000-3,500 crore of its own non-convertible debentures, shortly after releasing an earlier batch of pledged shares.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a mining and metal-refining business - it digs up zinc-lead ore, mostly in Rajasthan, and turns it into refined metal and silver (a valuable byproduct). The tension: reported profit has surged (Q1 FY27 net profit more than doubled), but by the company's own breakdown, that surge came almost entirely from higher global metal and silver prices and a weaker rupee - not from digging up or selling much more metal. So the business is doing fine operationally, but how much money it makes swings hard with commodity prices it doesn't control. It is also not a simple standalone company - its parent Vedanta borrows against a majority of its shares, so HZL shareholders carry some of Vedanta's financial risk even though Hindustan Zinc itself has very little debt.
analysis.quarters: FY26 (year to March 2026): revenue ₹40,844 crore (+20% YoY), EBITDA ₹22,162 crore (+27%, 54% margin), net profit ₹13,832 crore (+34%). Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter): revenue ₹13,747 crore (+77% YoY), EBITDA ₹8,074 crore (+109%, margin up ~900bps to 59%), net profit ₹5,469 crore (+145% YoY). Management's own EBITDA bridge for Q1 shows ₹2,826 crore of the gain came from higher metal prices and ₹980 crore from a favourable rupee, versus only ₹288 crore from higher volumes and ₹62 crore from cost improvement - so this was overwhelmingly a price/currency story, not a volume or efficiency one. Q2 FY27 (Sept quarter) production was a record (264 kt saleable metal, +7% YoY; silver +20%), but the matching financial numbers are not out yet - due October 19, 2026.
analysis.performance_read: The stock has strongly outperformed over 3 and 5 years (87.8%/113.2% vs Nifty's 16.8%/25.3%, and well ahead of peer Vedanta too), and is up 8.5% over the past year even as the Nifty fell 9.5%. That said, it sits 24.7% below its May 2024 peak of ₹717. There is no demerger or bonus distorting this - the only corporate action on record is a 2011 5:1 split, already reflected in the price series - so the drawdown looks like a genuine commodity-price correction (zinc/silver cycle) rather than an artifact of a spin-off.
analysis.valuation_read: Trailing P/E is reported in the 13.5x-13.9x range by screener-style sources, roughly in line with or slightly above sector peers (~12-13x). Why it looks the way it does: the 'E' in that P/E is currently inflated by near-record zinc and especially silver prices, not by a structurally wider margin business. Whether it is cheap or expensive hinges entirely on whether you think today's metal price strength is durable - against the company's own very high ROE (~61%) and ROCE (~69%), it looks reasonably priced; against the risk that silver/zinc prices mean-revert from current highs, the multiple could look considerably higher once realised.
analysis.growth_read: Revenue and profit growth in FY26 and Q1 FY27 was almost entirely price-and-currency led, not volume-led - management's own numbers put ~95% of the Q1 EBITDA increase down to metal prices and the rupee, versus ~5% from volumes and costs combined. Underlying output is genuinely growing too (refined zinc/lead/silver all up mid-to-high single or double digits YoY in H1 FY27 on real capacity additions at Chanderiya, Dariba and Debari), but at a far slower pace than the headline profit growth - so the durability of this growth rate depends on commodity prices, not just execution.
analysis.health_read: FY26 operating cash flow of ₹17,008 crore comfortably covered capex of ₹5,262 crore, and debt-to-equity is low at roughly 0.39x with debt/EBITDA near 0.58x - profits are converting into real cash and the standalone balance sheet is not stretched. The risk to flag is not business risk (the mine-to-metal operation is profitable and cash generative) and not company-level debt risk, but a holding-structure risk: parent Vedanta has encumbered just over 50% of Hindustan Zinc's equity to secure its own debentures, meaning HZL shareholders are exposed to parent-level financial engineering that has nothing to do with HZL's own operations.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter Vedanta Ltd holds about 60.7% of Hindustan Zinc, and the Government of India retains a residual stake reported between roughly 28% and 29.5% (sources vary on the exact date-stamped figure) after periodically selling down - most recently about 1.6% in November 2025, with further stake-sale reports circulating for 2026. Of Vedanta's holding, just over 50% of HZL's total share capital is currently encumbered (a mix of a small pledge and larger non-disposal undertakings) against Vedanta's own borrowings, after an earlier tranche of pledged shares was released in September 2026 and promptly replaced by fresh encumbrance tied to new NCDs. No marquee independent institutional investor stands out in the available data; the free float is thin given promoter and government holdings together run near 90%.
strengths: FY26 ROCE of ~69% and ROE of ~61% are among the highest of any large Indian metals company
FY26 operating cash flow of ₹17,008 crore well exceeded capex of ₹5,262 crore, with debt/equity at a low ~0.39x
Record H1 FY27 output: saleable metal 524 kt (+6% YoY) and silver production up sharply (Q2 silver +20% YoY), backed by real capacity additions at Chanderiya, Dariba and Debari
3-year and 5-year stock returns (87.8% and 113.2%) have comfortably beaten the Nifty (16.8% and 25.3%) and peer Vedanta
watchpoints: Q1 FY27's 145% profit jump was ~95% attributable to higher metal prices and a weaker rupee per management's own bridge, with volume contributing only ₹288 crore of the ₹8,074 crore EBITDA - a reversal in silver/zinc prices would hit profit hard

Parent Vedanta has encumbered just over 50% of Hindustan Zinc's share capital (pledge + non-disposal undertakings) to secure its own debentures - a holding-company risk layered on an otherwise low-debt operating company
Government of India still holds a ~28-29.5% stake and has sold down periodically (most recently ~1.6% in November 2025), with further stake-sale reports for 2026 - a recurring supply overhang

Stock remains 24.7% below its May 2024 peak; the current ~13-14x trailing P/E assumes today's elevated metal and silver prices persist - a correction would compress both earnings and the multiple together
analysis.one_thing: The Q2 FY27 financial results and earnings call on October 19, 2026 - specifically whether revenue/margin growth is still almost entirely price-and-forex-driven (as in Q1) or whether the record H1 volume growth is starting to contribute meaningfully, and any management commentary on sustaining current metal/silver price levels.
analysis.data_notes: FY26 annual figures (revenue ₹40,844 cr, EBITDA ₹22,162 cr, PAT ₹13,832 cr) and Q1 FY27 figures (revenue ₹13,747 cr, EBITDA ₹8,074 cr, PAT ₹5,469 cr) were cross-checked across multiple independent sources (Business Standard, Investing.com, Whalesbook, Udaipur Times) and were consistent. Q2 FY27 production data is from the company's own production update; Q2 financial results are not yet out (due Oct 19, 2026). Valuation ratios (P/E 13.5x-13.9x, ROE ~61%, ROCE ~69%, debt/equity ~0.39x) came from screener-style aggregators and varied slightly by source/date - treat as approximate; recommend checking Screener.in post-results for exact current figures. Government of India's stake was reported as both 27.92% and 29.54% across sources depending on reporting date - flagged as a range rather than a single verified number. No evidence found of a marquee independent institutional investor on the register.
